---
title: "How the work is documented"
description: "Dates, evidence and limits behind the journal."
---

## A date is not a single thing

Each post will distinguish the **coverage date** assigned to the story, the
period the observations describe, the data vintage or cutoff, the actual
analysis date, the actual publication date and the precise code revision.
Unknown values stay unknown.

Coverage dates begin on June 14, 2023 and fall on Wednesdays through June 9,
2027. They organize the archive; they do not establish that work happened on
those dates. A final portfolio summary is planned separately for June 2027.

## Evidence before conclusions

Verified historical work will be linked to dated evidence. A newly executed
retrospective analysis will say when it was performed and what older data it
used. Future work remains excluded from the published site; it cannot contain
invented outcomes. Sources, limitations and the exact analysis code revision
will accompany each published result. No analysis revisions are linked yet
because none have been verified for a published post.

For example, the grocery workbooks contain a June 13, 2023 ALFRED vintage
covering January 2018 through May 2023, but the workbook files were created in
November 2026. That distinction matters when describing any retrospective
analysis.

## Small, reproducible steps

A weekly milestone is planned around approximately two hours **in total**,
including analysis, focused validation and writing. This is a budget, not a
claim about hours already worked. Not every coverage slot has a distinct
milestone, and unassigned slots will not become filler posts.

Published figures will be curated, stable exports rather than figures
regenerated from changing notebooks during the site build. Figures will include
captions and meaningful alternative text; result tables will have clear
headings and units.

## Boundaries that matter

The electricity data describes one household, not a population or a current
bill. The original 2025 Week 8 fantasy matchup analysis is excluded because
its defense input duplicates the previous week's file; missing slot/wide data
will not be reconstructed. Learning results will use privacy-reviewed
aggregates only. Learner-level records and clickstream data are not published
or required.
